subject: Deployment mode & pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Paul Hart <paul.hart@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode discussion — recap & next steps

Hi Paul — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have shared signals: 

- Primary workload: document ingestion + question answering for clinician workflows (PHI scope).
- Expected steady-state: ~1k requests/day (~350–500k tokens/day). Peak: ~50 qps during business hours for short queries, occasional longer-context runs for chart summarization.
- Latency SLO: <300 ms for user-facing queries; offline batch jobs can be higher.
- Security/regulatory: must support HIPAA, customer-managed keys, and network isolation options.
- Decision timeline: aiming for vendor selection by end of Q2, procurement & security review running in parallel.

Given the above, three deployment modes are viable — rough tradeoffs we discussed: 
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted): lowest time-to-value and simplest ops. Per-token billing; no infra commit. Good for early pilots or if you want no infra ownership.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pool with isolation and predictable throughput. Best fit if you need steady throughput and want lower unit-cost at scale (reserved commits).
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): for strict regulatory controls and full network isolation. Higher up-front cost (infrastructure + license) but meets strict PHI controls.

Next steps I propose:
- Can you confirm the average tokens per request (approx)? I used 500 tokens/request as a baseline.
- Confirm whether procurement prefers a single contract for hosting vs a reserved capacity commit.
- I can run a simple ballpark cost model for each mode (per-token hosted vs. monthly reserved capacity vs. private deployment TCO) and share by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: deployment_assumptions.xlsx (assumptions tab), pricing_summary.pdf (high-level model)

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

From: Paul Hart <paul.hart@acmehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode discussion — recap & next steps

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Tokens/request: rough average 450 tokens for a standard query, but long-form summarization jobs can be ~2k tokens (maybe 10% of traffic).
- Daily volumes right now are modest (1k requests/day) but we expect 3x growth in 6–9 months if the pilot succeeds.
- PHI: yes, this is a must — if Hosted API can meet our BAAs + customer-managed KMS + VPC egress controls, it would be simplest. If not, Dedicated or Private are on the table.
- Procurement: Emily (cc'd) will run procurement timing — likely needs a formal SOW and cost estimate to engage.

Can you include a very concrete ballpark: 3 scenarios (pilot hosted, 6-month dedicated pilot, private deployment one-time + monthly ops) so procurement can compare? We just need order-of-magnitude numbers to decide next internal steps.

Paul
Paul Hart
Director of Clinical Innovation, Acme Health
paul.hart@acmehealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Paul Hart <paul.hart@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode discussion — ballpark cost models attached

Paul / Emily — thanks. Attached is a short ballpark model (ballpark_cost_model.csv) and a 1-page pricing summary. High-level numbers (very approximate — final pricing depends on model choice, committed capacity, and exact throughput):

- Scenario A — Hosted API (pilot):
  - Assumptions: 1k requests/day, avg 500 tokens/request => ~15M tokens/month.
  - Ballpark: $0.0006 / token => ~$9,000 / month. No infra commit, includes managed updates, SOC2, standard BAAs.

- Scenario B — Dedicated reserved capacity (6-month pilot):
  - Assumptions: one medium pool (2x A100-equivalent rented as reserved) providing baseline throughput with headroom.
  - Ballpark: Reserved commit ~ $25k–$35k / month (discounted with 6-month commitment). Unit cost/token drops significantly for sustained high throughput and lower tail latency. Includes private capacity, KMS integration, and stricter network isolation.

- Scenario C — Private VPC / On-prem (TCO):
  - Assumptions: initial infra + deployment + licensing + ops ramp.
  - Ballpark: one-time setup ~$120k–$200k (hardware + config + validation) + monthly ops/support ~$8k–$12k. Best for strict regulatory + long-term cost control at very large scale.

Trade-offs and notes:
- Hosted gives fastest time-to-value but is per-token; if you cross sustained volumes, Dedicated becomes more economical.
- Dedicated requires procurement for reserved commit; we can structure a 3–6 month pilot with a reduced introductory rate and then convert to standard reserved pricing.
- Private has highest up-front but allows full control and can be amortized for multi-year commitments.

Next actions I recommend:
1) Confirm whether the pilot should be hosted or Dedicated — I can build a month-by-month cashflow for both.
2) If Dedicated is preferred, we can propose a 6-month pilot with an introductory 20% credit on the first two months to reduce risk.
3) If procurement wants a SOW, Emily — I can draft a one-page SOW + statement of work and timeline.

Attachment: ballpark_cost_model.csv (cost by month, assumptions)

Let me know which scenario you want me to expand, and I’ll produce a line-item estimate for procurement.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Deployment mode discussion — pricing follow-up (Acme Health)

Marissa / Vivek — FYI and ask. Acme (Paul + Emily) are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. They have PHI requirements and modest initial volume but expect 3x growth. I shared ballpark numbers (see forwarded thread).

Recommendation: propose a 6-month Dedicated pilot with an introductory pricing structure: 20% credit on months 1–2, then standard reserved pricing for months 3–6. This lowers procurement friction and demonstrates the economics vs Hosted. If they insist on Hosted, we position it as a rapid pilot with a conversion path to Dedicated once volumes justify commits.

Can you: 
- Marissa: confirm whether 20% intro credit on a 6-month pilot is approvable from a pricing perspective.
- Vivek: if yes, can you prepare an internal quote (pricing summary + SOW) we can send to Emily for procurement?

I attached the ballpark_cost_model.csv and pricing_summary.pdf for reference.

Thanks — aiming to get a formal SOW request into procurement next week.

-Aditya
